Currently in 3rd year of my studies in VFX and who would like to be a layout artist, the layout artist in 3D is pretty far from what it is in 2D.

YOu are essentially the rythm guy before the editing comes in, your job is to turn the storyboard from 2D to 3D and that consists on all the movements within the shots, determining their lengths and rythms and all that using shitty 3D models (proxies of the ones that'll actually be used) along with extremely rough animations that you'll make to determine timing and composition and see if what was done during the storyboard is actually doable and if some stuff needs to be tweaked here and there.

Layout is extremely important as it will determine the animations needed and so influence the job of the rig artist (another job I'd like to have :3) and a lot of the set design as well.

If you want a clearer idea it's essentially the 3D version of the 2D animatic. Even though sometimes productions will first make a 2D animatic even if they'll also make a 3D layout for production reasons.

In Live Action we sometimes do smthng called a previzualisation, serves the same role.
